Documentation → Administration → Audit log

Audit log

The read-only trail of who did what, when, from where and against which target — searchable by user, action, text, entry ID and date.

👤 ForAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsaudit.view
📍 WhereAdministrator → Audit Log (every ADOM) (URL /audit/)

What is it?#

The Audit Log is SATOM's record of actions taken in the console and through the API: sign-ins and sign-outs, configuration changes, device actions, token management, theme edits, failures and more. Each entry names the user, the action, the target, a detail payload, the client IP address and the time. The page is read-only — there is no control to edit or delete an entry, for anyone.

What does it do?#

  • Lists entries newest first, 50 per page by default.
  • Filters by free-text search, Username, Action and a date range, and pages through the result with Previous / Next.
  • Exports the entries matching the current filters as a CSV file.
  • Finds a single entry again by its entry ID (#4821, 4821 or AUD-004821).
  • Opens a detail panel per entry with the full payload and, for failures, the Error reference you can look up in the server log.
  • Scopes entries to the active ADOM.

Requirements#

None. Entries are written automatically by the features that perform actions.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

The page requires audit.view, and the Audit Log sidebar link is shown only to users who hold it. The three system profiles (Viewer, Operator and Administrator) all include it. A user whose profile lacks audit.view does not see the link and is refused at /audit/.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the Audit Log requires audit.view (custom profiles without it lose access), pages with Previous / Next, includes the whole To Date day, and Export CSV downloads the filtered entries.

How to use#

Browse the log#

  1. Open Administrator → Audit Log.
  2. The table shows ID, Timestamp, User, Action, Target, Detail and IP Address. Action badges are coloured: red for actions containing delete or error, green for create or login, blue for update or backup, grey otherwise.
  3. Click anywhere on a row (except the ID) to open the Audit Entry panel on the right. Close it with the × button, by clicking outside it, or with Esc.
  4. Click Refresh to reload the page.
  5. Below the table, Page N / M with Previous and Next moves through the result. The filters are kept from page to page.

Filter the log#

  1. In the Filters card fill in any of: - Search (user · action · target · detail · error ID) — matches any part of the username, action, target or detail. A value that looks like an entry ID also matches that entry. - Username — the exact username. - Action — one of Login, Logout, Create, Update, Delete, Backup, Error, API Call. This matches any action whose name contains the word, so Create also finds api_token.create. - From Date / To Date.
  2. Click Apply. The count line reads Showing N entries (filtered).
  3. Click Clear to remove all filters.

The Quick search… box above the table only hides rows on the page you are looking at; it does not query the database.

Export entries as CSV#

  1. Set the filters you want (or none) and click Apply.
  2. Click Export CSV. The browser downloads audit-log.csv with the entries matching the current filters, newest first, up to 50,000 rows.
  3. The columns are id, timestamp_utc, username, action, target, ip_address, product (the ADOM) and extra (the detail). A text cell that starts with =, +, - or @ is prefixed with ' so a spreadsheet does not run it as a formula.

Find an entry again by its ID#

  1. Click the #ID in the first column — it is copied to the clipboard (the label briefly shows copied ✓) and the panel does not open.
  2. Paste it into Search later and click Apply. 4821, #4821 and AUD-004821 all find the same entry. A plain number still matches targets and details that contain it, too.

Trace a failure#

When an entry records an unhandled error, the panel opens with a red Error reference — an eight-character code such as 69881E81 — and a Copy button. Give that code to whoever has shell access to the node: it appears in the application log next to the full traceback. You can also paste the code into Search to find the entry.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Search Case-insensitive substring over username, action, target and detail; plus entry-ID match. No api_token
Username Exact username of the acting user. No jdoe
Action Substring of the action name (see list above). No Delete
From Date Entries at or after 00:00 of this date. No 2026-09-01
To Date Entries up to the end of this date (the whole day is included). No 2026-09-30
per_page (URL only) Entries per page, 10–200. No ?per_page=200
page (URL only) Page number. No ?page=2

Example#

🧪Example — Who revoked an API token?

  1. Open Administrator → Audit Log.
  2. Type api_token.revoke in Search and click Apply.
  3. The matching rows show the administrator in User, token:<public-id> in Target and the token's name in Detail.
  4. Click the row to see the IP address and the full detail payload.

Result#

The log only grows: SATOM has no screen or scheduled task that removes audit entries.

Troubleshooting#

Entries near midnight are missing from my date range#

Possible causes - Dates are compared with the stored UTC time, while the table shows times in the console's configured time zone.

Solution 1. Widen the range by one day on the side where entries are missing.

Verification - The entries appear.

The CSV export has fewer rows than the filter matches#

Possible causes - One export is capped at 50,000 rows.

Solution 1. Narrow the date range and export in several parts.

Verification - The last row of each file is older than the first row of the next.

An action I know happened is not in the log#

Possible causes - The entry belongs to another ADOM. A FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer or FortiAuthenticator session sees only that ADOM's entries; FortiWeb sees FortiWeb entries plus unscoped ones; Global sees everything. - The action was taken on an HA standby node, whose database is read-only; audit writes there are dropped silently. - Username is an exact match on an existing user: entries of a deleted user cannot be found with it.

Solution 1. Switch to the Global ADOM and search again. 2. Use Search with the username instead of the Username field.

Verification - The entry appears.

Advanced#

Advanced What an entry stores

Each row in the audit_logs table holds: an auto-increment ID, the user ID and username (anonymous when nobody is signed in, system outside a request), the action name (e.g. api_token.create, settings.theme.activate, login, ERROR), a target, a detail text, the IP address, the ADOM the action was performed in, and a UTC timestamp.

  • The detail is written as the text form of a key/value dictionary, not as strict JSON.
  • The IP address is the real client address resolved through the configured reverse proxy, not the proxy's own address.
  • Writing an entry is best-effort: if the database rejects it (for example on a read-only standby) the action itself still completes.
  • Failures recorded by the global error handler are written as action ERROR with error_id, exception type and message in the detail, de-duplicated per error ID. They carry no ADOM, so they are visible from FortiWeb and Global sessions.
  • Entries are ordered by timestamp, then by ID, so rows written in the same second keep a stable order across pages.
